key_insight: Measurement-driven ensemble phase transitions reveal changes in quantum-state ergodicity that remain invisible to maximally mixed first moments.
engineering_relevance: The results identify how bulk and final-boundary measurements can steer a quantum subsystem, informing measurement-based state-ensemble generation.
method: Study an ancillary qubit entangled with a system evolving under unitary gates and projective measurements.
Compare trajectory ensembles conditioned on circuit outcomes with projected ensembles from final system measurements.
Analyse ensemble transitions and quantum-design properties in Haar-random and Clifford circuits.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports non-analytic changes in both ensembles at the purification critical point, with distinct Haar-random and Clifford ensemble structures, but gives no numerical sizes or uncertainties.
watch_item: Clifford dynamics restrict ensemble expressivity: the projected ensemble reaches only a 1-design, while the trajectory ensemble forms designs up to order 3.
paper_title: Ensemble phase transitions in measurement-unitary hybrid quantum circuits
